items.title: Beat Battles v0 at the console
items.why: Beat battles are the brief's headline multiplayer mode. They only work once shared playback, reactions, a fair shared brief and server-checked unlocks all exist, and those come from M1-M2 and the Daily Brief. Scope: (a) A 'Start battle' prompt on the console opens a 30 s join window for 2 players. (b) Both players get the same brief and BPM, using only features both have unlocked, plus 90-180 s in their own beat maker. (c) Both beats play back to back through the NowPlaying slot; other broadcasts are blocked meanwhile. (d) Each listener gets one FIRE vote, with no voting for yourself. (e) The winner gets XP and a battle win. (f) A weekly top-producers board (OrderedDataStore) goes on the control-room mid wall, kept separate from OK's credits wall. Update 09_qa and t06 for the new interaction kind.
items.done_check: A server-side simulation with two fake entrants and three fake voters runs join, build, play A, play B, vote and result. It rejects self-votes and double votes, awards the winner once, and blocks outside broadcasts. A 3-player Local Server run completes one real round.

reviews.summary: The panels look good on desktop, but players get almost no guidance or feedback. There is no HUD and no goals. Two of the three XP sources pay out without telling the player, two messages are untrue, and the Profile tab can now only be reached from the credits wall. The beat maker, the main feature, only really works with a mouse: rows are about 22 px tall on phones, the character keeps walking while you edit, a gamepad cannot select anything, and Clear has no undo.

proposals.title: Honest feedback copy, visible XP, and signage fixes
proposals.what:
(a) In 06_runtime.lua, change the console toast to "Console on · +5 XP". Show the XP part only when XP was actually awarded. In the same change, give Console a 60 s per-player XP cooldown, mirroring DAWConfig.XPCooldown (10_daw.lua L22); today every toggle awards 5 XP. (b) In micTake, the start toast becomes "REC · 8s · +10 XP". The end toast becomes "Take done" instead of "Take saved to session", because nothing is stored. (c) DataService sets M.Persistent = true on the first successful GetAsync in Load. DAW_Save returns persisted = M.Persistent. DAWClient then shows "Saved · +10 XP" when persisted, and "Saved for this session (place not published yet)" otherwise. (d) The third lounge-TV screen changes from "DAW · COMING SOON…" to "OK BEAT MAKER

CONTROL ROOM · STUDIO PC
[F] MAKE A BEAT". (e) The Sessions tab drops the made-up line "Session wegonebeok_001 142 BPM F# minor". It shows the player's own beat from payload.profile.daw ("Your beat: 150 BPM · saved 3×"), or "No beat saved yet. Studio PC, control room." (f) Poster_A (x 37.5 to 41.7) and Poster_B (x 38.0 to 42.2) sit on the same plane and overlap, so the text z-fights and comes out garbled. Make each 3.4 studs wide, at x 36.8 to 40.2 and x 40.5 to 43.9. Their text does not change: whether masked titles stay or go remains the user's decision and is not part of this item. (g) The panel footer gains "Backspace / B to close". Tests: t07_play_client asserts the console and mic toasts contain "XP". t10 asserts the save status contains "session" when DataStore is unavailable.
proposals.player_moment: A player powers the console and sees "Console on · +5 XP" instead of a silent gain, then the lounge TV sends them to the beat maker instead of saying it is coming soon.
proposals.why: Players learn the rules from feedback. Today two XP sources pay out silently, two messages are untrue (a take is "saved"; a beat says "Saved" even though nothing lasts beyond the session), and the TV advertises the main feature as unreleased. This is the cheapest change with the widest effect.

proposals.title: Beat maker feel pass: audition, hit flash, beat ruler, safe Clear
proposals.what: In 10_daw.lua DAWUI and DAWClient: (a) Audition. When a cell is turned on, call engine:Trigger(t) once. Make each track label a TextButton that plays its sample on tap. (b) Hit flash. When the playhead reaches an on cell, flash it white and tween back to the track colour over about 0.12 s (or pulse a UIScale from 1.12 to 1). This replaces the current 0 vs 0.2 transparency difference, and the playhead column gets brighter. (c) Beat ruler. Add a 16-slot header row above the grid with the numbers 1-4 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13, and a lit dot that follows the Step attribute. (d) Safe Clear. Clear becomes UNDO for 4 s after use (it restores the previous Pattern), and Save moves to the far right of the transport, away from Clear. (e) Drag-paint. Pressing a cell and dragging across others sets them all to the new state (grid InputBegan/InputChanged), which makes 16th-note hats one gesture on touch. Tests: extend t10_play_client so that Command "clear" then "undo" restores the pattern, and an audition while stopped increments Hits.
proposals.player_moment: A new player taps a square and hears the snare at once, drags across the hat row to fill it, and sees each hit flash white as the playhead passes.
proposals.why: Today a toggle makes no sound until Play, a hit differs from a non-hit by only 20% transparency, there is no beat ruler, and Clear wipes all 64 steps with no undo, sitting right next to Save. Every step sequencer players know (BandLab, Incredibox-style Roblox music games) does these things. They are what make v0 feel like an instrument rather than a form.
proposals.evidence: 10_daw.lua DAWUI cell click L100 (toggle only, no sound); render() L104-111 (hit shown as transparency 0 vs 0.2, L110); track labels are TextLabels at L95; transport order L84-89 puts CLEAR beside SAVE; C.Clear L123 has no undo; captures/beat_maker_in_play.jpg (grey playhead column, hits barely distinguishable).

proposals.title: Sit at the desk: the PC seats you and frames the console
proposals.what: In the Systems.DAW Computer handler (10_daw.lua L174): if ControlRoom.Chair_Seat.Occupant is nil, call Chair_Seat:Sit(humanoid) and send seated = true with OpenDAW. In DAWClient, when seated: set the camera to Scriptable and tween it over 0.4 s to a fixed over-the-shoulder CFrame, about (68.5, 7.5, -2) looking at (75, 4.5, -2), so Screen_Main, the speakers and the 48 console meters fill the top of the screen. If the chair is taken, the current free-standing window and 14-stud walk-away close are used instead. WASD or the thumbstick still walks you, drifting 14 studs closes the beat maker, and the camera can end up facing the ceiling, which hides the meter pulse built for this feature. The brief asks that players "sit down" and "use computers". This connects the two and makes the room the backdrop to the feature.

proposals.title: Phone layout for the beat maker
proposals.what: Add a compact layout in DAWUI.Build when UserInputService.TouchEnabled is true and workspace.CurrentCamera.ViewportSize.Y < 600. The root fills the safe area (Size 1,-24,1,-24). Transport becomes a 64 px left column: a large PLAY, BPM − / value / +, SAVE, CLEAR/UNDO and CLOSE. The grid takes the rest of the screen. If the computed cell width is under 44 px, show 8 steps per page with a "1-8 | 9-16" pager that follows the playhead while playing. While the window is open, set GuiService.TouchControlsEnabled = false so the thumbstick and jump button do not sit over the outer steps, and restore it on close. This pairs with the seated mode in "Sit at the desk", so no movement is needed. Re-run the layout on ViewportSize changes (rotation). Test in Studio device emulation at 667×375 and 844×390: a client check asserts every Cell AbsoluteSize is at least 44×44 and every button is at least 44 px tall.
proposals.player_moment: On a phone the beat maker opens edge to edge with thumb-sized pads, the player flips between steps 1-8 and 9-16, and never jumps or walks away by accident.
proposals.why: Most Roblox sessions are on phones. The root is 0.92×0.6 of the screen with MinSize 340×230 and MaxSize 980×420, and the grid is the root minus 102 px. On a landscape phone about 390 pt tall, the window clamps to around 230 px. The four rows then get about 22 px each after the 10 px inset, and each cell is 18-36 px wide depending on screen width. That is half the usual 44 px touch target, and the window's lower half shares the screen with Roblox's thumbstick and jump button. As built, the main feature is effectively desktop-only.
proposals.evidence: 10_daw.lua DAWUI root Size and UISizeConstraint L72-74; grid Size (1,-32,1,-102) at L90; cell Size (span/nS,-4,1/nT,-10) at L98; build/*.lua has no TouchEnabled or GuiService code (grep); README.md and the brief both say "Phone/touch layout untested".

proposals.title: HUD chip: level, XP bar, Profile button, level-up moment
proposals.what: Add a new Modules.HUD, built by ClientMain into OK_UI. It is a top-left chip just below the Roblox top bar, containing: a "LVL 3" badge in UITheme.accent; a 120×6 px XP bar in accent2 showing (xp % LevelSize) / LevelSize; and a 44×44 "OS" button. The button fetches the profile through ProfileFunction and calls panel.Open("Profile", {profile = …}) with no source, so the panel does not auto-close on distance. On the server, DataService.AddXP sets player attributes Level and XP (these replicate for free). When the level rises, it fires InteractionEvent "LevelUp" {level}. On the client, a change to the XP attribute floats "+N XP" next to the bar, and LevelUp shows a centred 2 s banner ("LEVEL 3") with a short chime. The chime is a Roblox licensed-library sound, checked the same way the samples were (PlaybackLoudness check, as in t10_play_client.lua). The Profile tab gains the same bar and "N XP to level X+1". Show any "next unlock" text only once the progression work defines unlocks. Test: a client play script asserts the HUD is visible, the XP attribute rises after the console, and the OS button opens Profile.
proposals.player_moment: After saving their first beat, the player watches the bar fill and "LEVEL 2" flash across the screen, and from then on can tap OS anywhere to open their producer profile.
proposals.why: Systems.DAW took over the Computer interaction, so Profile and Sessions can now only be reached by walking to the credits wall. XP has no on-screen presence and level-ups happen silently. A persistent top-left chip is the usual Roblox convention, and it is the surface that tycoon, battles and other future systems will report into.

proposals.title: First-session checklist with a highlighted next target
proposals.what: Add Modules.Onboarding on the client, with progress stored server-side in the profile as profile.onboarding = {step, skipped}. On a player's first join, show a one-line welcome card ("OK STUDIO · prod. OK · make your first beat" with Start and Skip buttons). Then a four-step tracker appears inside the HUD chip: 1) Open the control room door (Door Open becomes true); 2) Make a beat at the studio PC (OpenDAW, then Playing); 3) Save your beat (DAW_Save returns ok); 4) Cut a take in the booth (Mic). Each step completes from the existing server event points (InteractionService hook, DAW_Save handler), and the server fires InteractionEvent "Goal" {step}. No images are needed, and only one Highlight exists at a time. Finishing all four shows a banner and awards a one-time +25 XP. The tracker can be collapsed, and returning players who have finished it never see it. proposals.why: Players spawn in the corridor and the sliding door starts closed, so the beat maker is two rooms away behind a closed door. Its prompts only appear within 8 studs, and nothing says what the place is for. A first-time tutorial with a skip option is the same thing the Boost Ball creator asked for in his final quality pass.

reviews.summary: Today a new player has no direction in minute 1: they spawn in the corridor with no goal, and level/XP only show in the credits wall's Profile tab, because Systems.DAW replaced the Computer handler. Minute 5 is a 4x16 loop only the maker hears. Minute 30 has nothing to chase (levels unlock nothing, and console XP can be farmed by spamming E), and there is no day 2 yet: the place is unpublished, and once it is, one failed DataStore read would overwrite a saved profile. The loop should run: make a beat, play it on the monitors for the room, earn XP and fires, unlock sounds and slots, come back for the daily brief. Build order: (1) next session: trustworthy XP and saves, playback on the monitors, the tour quest; (2) after that: beat format v2 with a beat library, level unlocks, the daily brief; (3) later: booth collab, producer cards, battles; (4) tycoon and customizable studios go last, because they need a currency and space for each player.

proposals.title: Make XP and saves trustworthy before levels mean anything
proposals.what: Next session. (a) XP: route every award through one gate, DataService.AddXP(player, n, source), using a new Config.XP.Sources table of {xp, cooldown} per source. Values: Console 5 XP at most once per 10 min per player. Mic take 10 XP at most once per 2 min per player. DAW save 10 XP only when the pattern differs from the last saved one and has at least 4 active cells (the 60 s cooldown stays). Ambient XP (console plus mic) is capped at 60 per UTC day. After every award, AddXP fires InteractionEvent 'Progress' {xp, level, gained, levelUp}, so any HUD the UI lens builds can render it; today the client never learns its XP except through the beat maker status line. (b) Saves: DataService.Load marks the profile loaded only when GetAsync succeeded (a nil result for a new player counts as success) and retries 3 times with backoff. Save skips profiles that never loaded, writes through UpdateAsync, and strips internal fields first. Add an autosave loop every 120 s next to the existing PlayerRemoving and BindToClose saves. Extend t07/t10 with these checks: 20 fast console presses give 5 XP, an identical re-save gives 0 XP, and a simulated failed load blocks Save.
proposals.player_moment: Day 2: a player who reached level 4 yesterday rejoins and is still level 4, instead of finding a fresh level-1 profile because one DataStore read failed.
proposals.why: Today XP can't be trusted: consolePower awards +5 on every toggle with no cooldown and HoldDuration 0, so spamming E gives a level every 20 presses. And after publish, DataService.Load (l.151) falls back to defaults when GetAsync fails, then Save (l.155) calls SetAsync over the real record when the player leaves, wiping it. Any unlock, streak or leaderboard built on this is either farmable or erasable. It's small and blocks everything else in the loop.

proposals.title: Play your beat on the studio monitors for the whole room, with fire reactions
proposals.what: Next session. Add a 'PLAY ON MONITORS' button to the beat maker transport bar. It calls a new Remotes.DAW_Broadcast. The server checks the pattern with Systems.DAW.Validate, rate-limits each player to one broadcast per 45 s, keeps a queue of at most 3, then sets a server-owned NowPlaying record (attributes on ReplicatedStorage.OK.NowPlaying: OwnerId, OwnerName = DisplayName, Pattern, BPM, StartAt = workspace:GetServerTimeNow() + 0.5, Bars = 8, PlayId). A new NowPlayingClient on every client runs a second DAWEngine whose step comes from (GetServerTimeNow() - StartAt), so all clients stay in sync. It parents the sample clones to Speaker_L and Speaker_R, so the sound is 3D, instead of SoundService. ClientMain's meter condition (l.322) also lights up while NowPlaying is active, so every player sees the console meters and speaker LEDs pulse. The lounge TV handler shows 'NOW PLAYING · prod. <DisplayName> · <BPM> BPM' while a beat plays. Its stale third screen 'DAW · COMING SOON' is replaced. During a play, each listener within about 40 studs gets one FIRE reaction, counted on the server. The owner gets +2 XP per fire, capped at 20 XP per play and 100 per day, so alt accounts can't farm it. profile.plays and profile.fires are counted. Uses 0 new lights and only existing parts. Test: two clients in play mode, both report the same step within one 16th note, and a second broadcast inside 45 s is refused.
proposals.player_moment: Minute 5: you press PLAY ON MONITORS, the people on the couch and in the lounge hear your beat through the speakers, the TV reads NOW PLAYING · prod. you · 150 BPM, and two of them hit FIRE.
proposals.why: Right now making a beat is a single-player toy (README: plays only for the player using it). Playing your beat for a room is what makes a studio feel like a multiplayer music game. It also builds the pieces every later system needs: a server-timed shared playback slot (battles play beats back to back in it), a reaction count (battle votes, producer rankings) and a reason to bring friends. The parts already exist: speakers, meters, TV, 12 seats.

proposals.title: Beat format v2 with 808, hat rolls, swing, mute and a 6-slot beat library (one migration)
proposals.what: Session after next. Replace the single 64-character string with profile.beats = {v=2, active=1, slots={{name, bpm, swing, mutes, tracks={Kick, Snare, Clap, Hat, Bass808}}}}. Each track is 16 characters. Drums use [01]. Hat uses [0-3], where 2 or 3 is a roll that fires 2 or 3 evenly spaced hits inside the step (the trap/plugg hat roll). Bass808 uses '.' for off and [0-9ab] for a semitone offset: the engine sets PlaybackSpeed = 2^(n/12), plays mono (each new 808 note stops the previous one) and uses a 0.6 s gate. Swing 0-60% delays every even 16th by swing x interval / 2. Per-track mute is saved. Validate checks each track's length and alphabet instead of total length. Migration runs once on load: an existing prof.daw.pattern becomes slot 1. Library: 3 slots at start, 6 at level 5 (item 5), with duplicate, clear and switch. Names are generated from neutral word lists (e.g. Midnight/Neon/Basement/Velvet/Static + Drift/Bounce/Loop/Wave/Run, plus the BPM) with a re-roll button: no free text, so no filtering, and no drug or profanity words. Sounds: search the Creator Store audio filtered to the Roblox APM / Pro Sound Effects partner library for an 808/sub hit, then check each candidate with the t10_play_client PlaybackLoudness test. Fallback: re-pitch the licensed APM kick 9043367885 with a long gate. Replace the unlicensed hat 140468458870544 in the same pass, because rolls make it the most audible sound. Extend t10_check for migration and per-track validation. 5 rows must still work on a phone (coordinate with the UI lens's phone layout).
proposals.player_moment: Minute 30: you open slot 3 'Velvet Drift · 150', write an 808 line that walks down three notes, put a triplet hat roll before the snare, swing it 30%, and the beat finally sounds like the music on the credits wall.
proposals.why: Four one-shot drums on one 16-step bar can't sound like OK's genre, which is built on pitched 808s and hat rolls, so there's nothing to get better at after a few minutes. And because one save slot is overwritten every time, a second idea erases the first. Validate requires exactly #Tracks x Steps characters, so adding any track breaks every existing save. Changing the format and adding slots together means the migration happens once.

reviews.lens: World, visuals, content and identity (desktop and phone)
reviews.summary: The rooms read as one orange-brown wash, and three things cause it. All 21 lights are omnidirectional PointLights that bleed through the 1-stud walls, the ceilings are pure black, and every surface sits at nearly the same value. On top of that, nothing in the world makes a sound (no Sound instance in 02-07). Only 3 light slots remain, so the richness has to come from neon parts, self-lit SurfaceGui text, materials, relief and sound, not from more lights; this also suits phones on low graphics quality. The question of what makes this feel like OK's world is answered by the three identity items (4, 5, 6). Approval-free means his public SoundCloud-era catalog voice, generic neon lettering and a readable record wall of Confirmed credits only. Leaks, private filenames, personal details and Unverified material are never used. His tag audio, beats, logo and any commercial use are gated on OK's team.

proposals.title: Light re-zoning: no bleed through walls, each room gets its own light (net +0 lights)
proposals.what: In 03_lighting.lua, make recessed() honor the angle it already receives. It should call L.light(lens, "SpotLight", color, bright, range, {Face = Enum.NormalId.Bottom, Angle = angle}) with range = ceiling height + 2 (about 14 for Spot_Console_1/2 and Spot_Couch, 12 for Spot_Booth), raising Brightness to compensate. Cap the remaining PointLights below the distance to the nearest shared wall (x=12, 44, 80). Pendant_Lounge_1/2 go to range 12-13 or become wide downward SpotLights. Lamp_Bulb goes to 6, Sconce_Booth and BoothLamp to 10-12. Sconce_Corridor and Uplight_Corridor go to 8-10, and Strip_Corridor becomes a downward SurfaceLight with range 10. Convert the wall-hung glows into SurfaceLights facing into their own room: Neon_Sign_Glow faces -X into the lounge and OK_Sign_Glow faces -X into the control room. Desk_LED (0.7/10) and Bar_LED (0.5/8) light almost nothing. Move one of them to the credits-wall wash (proposal 6) and the other to a console backlight behind the producer. The light count stays at 21. Add a check to 09_qa.lua: for each PointLight, assert Range <= distance to the nearest shared wall + 1; for each SpotLight with Face Bottom, assert Range <= height above floor + 3. Then re-capture every room from fixed camera spots (the current captures predate these passes). Do not present Shadows=true (BuildLib L.light sets it) as the fix, because ShadowMap ignores it for local lights.
proposals.player_moment: Walking from the lounge through the sliding door, the light changes at the threshold: warm pools over the console, pink at the sign. The same orange wash no longer leaks through every wall.
proposals.why: Today Spot_Couch (x=50, range 26) lights the lounge sofa through the mid wall. Spot_Console_1/2 (x=72, range 28) wash the whole booth through its wall. Pendant_Lounge_2 (x=32, range 22) reaches x=54 in the control room, and Pendant_Lounge_1 reaches into the corridor. So every room has the same flat light. Separate light per room is the cheapest step toward an impressive look, and it works under ShadowMap without the user switching to Future.

proposals.what: (1) Ceilings: change the Ceiling_* color in 02_shell.lua from C.black (12,12,14) to a dark warm grey (about 44,40,42) so the existing lights show the ceiling. Add 3-4 walnut beams and one duct cylinder in the lounge, and 3 floating fabric clouds with black edges at y 10.8 in the control room (about 25 parts). (2) Walls: move C.concrete from 30,30,32 to a cooler blue-grey (about 38,40,46) so warm pools and neon separate from the walls. Add a 0.4-stud black baseboard and a trim line at door height on every wall (about 30 parts). (4) Relief: rebuild the booth foam as charcoal wedge or pyramid tiles with alternating depth (0.2 / 0.5) and only occasional maroon tiles, about 180 parts. proposals.title: Licensed room ambience and acoustics: the studio stops being silent (+0 lights)
proposals.what: New idempotent build script 11_ambience.lua (OK_Build attribute) plus a small client module. It places looping Sound instances in existing parts, with RollOffMode InverseTapered and RollOffMaxDistance sized to each room. Lounge: a low vinyl-crackle bed and a quiet licensed hip-hop or trap instrumental bed (Volume about 0.15) from a speaker hidden in the TV wall. Control room: monitor hiss or HVAC room tone. Booth: near-silent room tone. Corridor: a muffled bass thump through an EqualizerSoundEffect low-pass, as if a session is running. On the client, set SoundService.AmbientReverb by which floor the player stands on: Booth gives PaddedCell, Lounge LivingRoom, Control Room, Corridor StoneCorridor. While SlidingDoor's Open attribute is false, cut the highs on the lounge bed for players in the control room. No asset IDs are invented here: search the Creator Store audio for APM / Pro Sound Effects licensed items ("room tone", "air conditioning", "vinyl crackle", "hip hop instrumental"). Verify each one in play by PlaybackLoudness, the way t10_play_client.lua does, and record SoundId plus source in a Config.Ambience table, as DAWConfig does. Optional second step: a "Spin a record" prompt on the existing record crates that cycles 3 licensed instrumentals server-side for everyone. The records are labeled as library tracks, never as OK's beats or credits. This adds an interaction kind, so update 09_qa.lua (asserts exactly 7 interactables) and t06_check.lua (asserts 7 kinds).
proposals.player_moment: Walking from the lounge into the booth, the music bed and crackle drop to a padded hush. Closing the sliding door turns the lounge into a distant thump.
proposals.why: The brief asks for a music universe, yet builds 02-07 contain no Sound instance; the only audio is the beat maker samples. Ambience does a lot for immersion per hour of work, costs no lights or parts, and stays inside the licensed-library limit.

reviews.lens: Social, multiplayer and Roblox platform readiness
reviews.summary: OK Studio runs on a multiplayer engine, but every player is alone in it. A beat only plays on the client of the player who made it (10_daw.lua line 41 parents each sample clone to SoundService). Nothing else is shared either: no common moment, no identity other players can see, no way to invite anyone, no analytics. Two bugs have to be fixed before strangers play. A failed profile load can overwrite the saved profile with defaults, and the prompts have no rate limit, so anyone can farm XP or keep flipping the lights and door that everyone shares. After those fixes, the most useful single build is playing a beat through the studio monitors for the whole room, because invites, producer tags and beat battles all depend on it. Publishing steps, the content rating, and anything involving OK's name or money stay with the user and OK's team.

proposals.title: Stop the profile loader from wiping saves
proposals.what: Rewrite Services.DataService in build/06_runtime.lua. (1) Load: try GetAsync up to 3 times with 1, 2 and 4 s backoff. If every attempt fails, cache the default profile with _loadFailed = true, toast "Progress could not load, this session will not save", and never write that profile. (2) Save: use UpdateAsync instead of SetAsync, and stamp each write with a schema version v = 1 and updatedAt. (3) Autosave changed profiles every 120 s. Change BindToClose to save all players in parallel with task.spawn, then wait for them to finish, instead of saving one after another. (4) Keep the last 5 saved beats in prof.beats as {pattern, bpm, t}. Today prof.daw holds one slot that each save overwrites; migrate it to beats[1] on load. Keep the existing in-memory fallback for Studio. (5) Add t11_check.lua. It injects a fake store whose GetAsync always errors and asserts that leaving never writes. A second fake asserts that autosave fires and that a changed profile goes through UpdateAsync.
proposals.player_moment: A returning player joined during a DataStore hiccup. When they come back the next day, their level and beats are still there instead of reset to level 1 with nothing saved.
proposals.why: Today M.Load wraps GetAsync in pcall. If that call fails, the player silently gets DEFAULT {level 1, xp 0}, and M.Save then writes that default over their real data with SetAsync on PlayerRemoving. One throttled read on join wipes a returning player. There is also no autosave, so a server crash loses the whole session. Players who lose progress do not come back, and this is much cheaper to fix before real data exists.
proposals.evidence: build/06_runtime.lua lines 149-155 (M.Load: pcall GetAsync, fall back to the default, then M.Save calls SetAsync with whatever was cached), line 162 (BindToClose saves one player after another, no autosave anywhere); build/10_daw.lua line 168 (prof.daw is a single slot that each save overwrites)
